title: Prototype-Debiased Latent Alignment for Class-Imbalanced EEG Decoding

contributions.purpose: Reveal and explain a previously untested failure mode of Latent Alignment (LA) under class-imbalanced context sets.
contributions.mechanism: Identify the prototype-mixture mean shift mechanism: LA subtracts a context mean that, under imbalance, becomes biased toward majority-class prototypes (mu_ctx = sum_c p_c mu_c + delta_s), causing systematic misalignment.
contributions.evaluation: On PhysioNet Sleep, LA weighted accuracy drops from balanced 0.7588 to MC WA 0.6664 (9.2pp gap), falling to 0.5219 at extreme imbalance (alpha=0.1); shift magnitude correlates with accuracy drop (r=0.518).
contributions.source_quote: We identify LA's vulnerability to class-imbalanced context sets and characterize the prototype-mixture mean shift mechanism causing this degradation.

contributions.purpose: Correct the class-mixture bias in the alignment statistics.
contributions.mechanism: Prototype-Debiased Latent Alignment (PD-LA): subtract a bias term b(p) = sum_c (p_hat_c - 1/C) mu_c from the context mean, using class prototypes mu_c computed from training data and estimated class proportions p_hat_c, preserving the subject-specific offset.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a correction formula; validated by oracle-prior recovery and correlation-drop analysis.
contributions.domain: Latent Alignment / label-shift correction for EEG
contributions.source_quote: We propose PD-LA, a correction formula that removes the class-mixture bias while preserving subject-specific adaptation.

contributions.purpose: Validate that the correction addresses the identified mechanism and recovers accuracy under oracle priors.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate PD-LA with oracle (ground-truth) priors on PhysioNet ME (3-class) and Sleep (5-class) using EEGNet/DeepSleepNet with LA layers; correlate shift vs accuracy drop before/after correction.
contributions.evaluation: Oracle PD-LA recovers 76% of the gap (+7.39pp MC WA, 0.6664->0.7403) and +20.86pp at alpha=0.1; shift-accuracy correlation drops r=0.518 -> -0.145 (delta r=0.663).
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that oracle PD-LA recovers 76% of the imbalance-induced accuracy gap (+7.4pp) and improves extreme-imbalance accuracy by +20.9pp.

contributions.purpose: Explain why the deployable (practical) variant fails, framing the open problem.
contributions.mechanism: Show LA's normalization makes predictions approximately invariant to context class composition, creating an identifiability problem that defeats standard label-shift prior estimators (soft-prob averaging, argmax counting).
contributions.evaluation: Predicted-prior PD-LA gains only +1.58pp on Sleep and -0.01pp on ME; estimator reliability r~0.23 pulls estimates toward uniform, rendering correction uninformative.
contributions.source_quote: We identify prior estimation as the key bottleneck: LA's normalization makes predictions invariant to context composition, limiting the practical variant's effectiveness.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Latent Alignment (Bakas et al., 2023) extends these ideas by performing subject-wise standardization at multiple layers within a deep network, formulated as a Deep Set (Zaheer et al., 2017) ... However, the original work notes a trade-off between alignment depth and susceptibility to class imbalance, a limitation we directly address in this paper.

Standard approaches for label shift estimation (Lipton et al., 2018; Garg et al., 2020) use model predictions ... We implement a predicted-prior variant (PD-LA Pred) that averages softmax outputs over the context set.
Our work addresses a related but distinct problem: correcting the bias in alignment statistics caused by class-imbalanced context sets, rather than adapting model parameters.
Following Bakas et al. (2023), we use EEGNet (Lawhern et al., 2016) for ME and DeepSleepNet (Supratak et al., 2017) for Sleep, both augmented with Latent Alignment layers.

notes: Honest negative results: the practical/deployable PD-LA variant barely helps (+1.58pp Sleep, -0.01pp ME) because prior estimation is fundamentally unidentifiable under LA's normalization; the ME benchmark shows almost no imbalance effect (0.32pp gap) so corrections are near-zero there; the headline +7.4pp/+20.9pp gains require an oracle (non-deployable) that uses ground-truth class proportions.
